title: Admin - Prevent Unauthorized Access - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Prevent Unauthorized Access feature on the Y4J platform. This feature restricts admin management actions (add admins, edit roles, edit permissions) to Super Admins only. Limited-access admins cannot access the User & Roles module, and unauthorized access returns an error message. Edge cases include manual URL entry, token expiration, and permission mismatch due to caching. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for error message accessibility, navigation restrictions, screen reader announcements, and accessible denial states.

testCases.title: Unauthorized access error message is announced by screen reader
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, attempts to access User & Roles module
steps: Log in as a Limited-Access Admin
Attempt to navigate to the User & Roles module (via navigation or direct URL)
Verify an error/denial message is displayed
Verify screen reader announces the error message immediately
Verify the message uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive' for immediate announcement
expectedResults: Error message is displayed clearly (e.g., 'You do not have permission to access this page')
Screen reader immediately announces the error (role='alert' or aria-live='assertive')
Message is announced without requiring the user to navigate to it
User understands they are denied access and why
testCases.postconditions: Unauthorized users are clearly informed of access denial

testCases.title: Error message text has sufficient color contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, unauthorized access error is displayed
steps: Trigger the unauthorized access error message
Use a contrast checker to measure error message text against its background
Check contrast of any heading text in the error page/message
Check contrast of any supplementary text or instructions
expectedResults: Error message text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
Heading text (if large) has at least 3:1 contrast ratio
All supplementary text meets 4.5:1 minimum
Text is readable for users with low vision

testCases.title: Error message does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, unauthorized access error is displayed
steps: Observe the error message/page visually
Check if the error state is conveyed through more than just color (e.g., icon, text prefix, border style)
View in grayscale mode
Verify the error is still identifiable without color
expectedResults: Error uses text message (not just a red indicator)
Error includes an icon or text prefix (e.g., 'Access Denied:' or lock icon with alt text)
In grayscale mode, error state is still clearly identifiable
Multiple visual cues convey the error state
testCases.postconditions: Error is perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Error page/message has proper heading structure
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, unauthorized access error page is displayed
steps: Navigate to the error page/message
Inspect the heading structure
Verify there is an H1 heading describing the error (e.g., 'Access Denied')
Verify any subheadings follow logical hierarchy
expectedResults: Error page has an H1 heading (e.g., 'Access Denied' or 'Unauthorized')
Heading hierarchy is sequential without skipping levels
Screen reader users can quickly identify the page purpose via heading navigation
Heading clearly communicates the denial state
testCases.postconditions: Error page has proper semantic structure

testCases.title: Error page has descriptive page title
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, unauthorized access error page is displayed
steps: Check the browser tab title when the error page is displayed
Verify the title describes the error state
Verify screen reader announces the page title on navigation
expectedResults: Page title includes error context (e.g., 'Access Denied - User & Roles')
Title is descriptive and unique
Screen reader announces the title, helping users understand they've been denied access
testCases.postconditions: Error page is identifiable by its title

testCases.title: User & Roles navigation item is hidden or disabled for Limited-Access Admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin
steps: Log in as a Limited-Access Admin
Navigate through the main navigation using keyboard and screen reader
Check if 'User & Roles' menu item is hidden, disabled, or absent
If hidden: verify it is not in the DOM or has aria-hidden='true'
If disabled: verify it has aria-disabled='true' and screen reader announces 'disabled'
expectedResults: User & Roles menu item is either completely hidden (not in Tab order, not announced by screen reader) OR visibly disabled with aria-disabled='true'
If hidden: not reachable via Tab, not announced by screen reader
If disabled: announced as 'disabled' by screen reader, not activatable
Limited-Access Admin is not confused by inaccessible navigation items
testCases.postconditions: Restricted navigation is properly communicated to assistive technology

testCases.title: Direct URL access denial is keyboard navigable
testCases.componentElement: Error page after direct URL access
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin
steps: Manually enter the User & Roles module URL in the browser address bar
Verify the error/denial page loads
Tab through all interactive elements on the error page (e.g., 'Go Back', 'Home' links)
Verify all elements are keyboard accessible
Verify there is a way to navigate away from the error page via keyboard
expectedResults: Error page loads when URL is manually entered
All interactive elements (links, buttons) on the error page are reachable via Tab
Navigation links (e.g., 'Go to Dashboard', 'Go Back') are keyboard activatable
User is not trapped on the error page
Focus indicator is visible on all interactive elements
testCases.postconditions: Error page is fully keyboard navigable

testCases.title: Token expiration error is announced accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, session token has expired
steps: Allow the session token to expire while on the User & Roles page
Attempt an admin management action (add admin, edit role, edit permissions)
Verify an error message about session expiration is displayed
Verify screen reader announces the error
Verify the error provides guidance (e.g., 'Please log in again')
expectedResults: Token expiration error is displayed clearly
Screen reader announces the error immediately (role='alert' or aria-live='assertive')
Error message explains the issue (e.g., 'Your session has expired. Please log in again.')
A link or button to log in again is provided and keyboard accessible
Error does not rely solely on color
testCases.postconditions: Token expiration is communicated accessibly with recovery path

testCases.title: Permission mismatch error (caching) is announced accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User's permissions have been changed (downgraded) while they are still logged in with cached permissions
steps: Simulate a permission mismatch (user's role was downgraded but cached session still shows old permissions)
Attempt an admin management action that the user no longer has permission for
Verify an error message is displayed
Verify screen reader announces the error
Verify the error provides guidance for resolution
expectedResults: Error message is displayed (e.g., 'Your permissions have changed. Please refresh the page.')
Screen reader announces the error immediately
Error provides actionable guidance (refresh, log out/in)
Error does not rely solely on color
Recovery action (refresh button/link) is keyboard accessible
testCases.postconditions: Permission mismatch is communicated with recovery guidance

testCases.title: Error page is readable at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: Unauthorized access error page is displayed
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify the error message is fully visible
Verify any navigation links/buttons are visible and usable
Verify no text is clipped or hidden
expectedResults: Error message text is fully readable at 200% zoom
Navigation links/buttons remain visible and usable
No text is clipped or hidden
No horizontal scrollbar for text content
testCases.postconditions: Error page is functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Error page reflows at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: Unauthorized access error page is displayed
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify error message content reflows without horizontal scrolling
Verify navigation links/buttons are accessible
Verify all text is readable
expectedResults: Error page content reflows to fit narrow viewport
No horizontal scrollbar required
All interactive elements remain accessible
Text is fully readable
testCases.postconditions: Error page works on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Error page has main landmark region
testCases.preconditions: Unauthorized access error page is displayed
steps: Use screen reader landmark navigation on the error page
Verify the page has a main landmark containing the error content
Verify navigation areas use nav landmark
expectedResults: Error page has a <main> or role='main' landmark
Error message content is within the main landmark
Screen reader users can jump to main content quickly
Navigation uses appropriate landmark
testCases.postconditions: Error page has proper landmark structure

testCases.title: Recovery navigation links have accessible names
testCases.componentElement: Recovery links/buttons on error page (Go Back, Dashboard, Login)
testCases.preconditions: Unauthorized access error page is displayed with recovery navigation
steps: Identify all recovery links/buttons on the error page (e.g., 'Go to Dashboard', 'Go Back', 'Log In Again')
Tab to each link/button
Verify each has an accessible name describing its destination/action
Verify screen reader announces the name and role
Activate each using Enter (links) or Enter/Space (buttons)
expectedResults: Each recovery link/button has a descriptive accessible name
Screen reader announces name and role (e.g., 'Go to Dashboard, link')
Links are activatable via Enter
Buttons are activatable via Enter and Space
Focus indicator is visible on each element

testCases.title: Restricted actions are not exposed to Limited-Access Admin in the DOM
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Limited-Access Admin, navigating pages they do have access to
steps: Log in as Limited-Access Admin
Navigate to pages the user does have access to
Verify that 'Add Admin', 'Edit Roles', and 'Edit Permissions' controls are not present in the DOM or are properly hidden
Use screen reader to scan for any admin management controls
Verify no hidden but focusable admin controls exist
expectedResults: Admin management controls are not rendered in the DOM for Limited-Access Admin
OR if rendered, they have aria-hidden='true' and tabindex='-1' (not focusable)
Screen reader does not announce any admin management controls
No hidden controls are reachable via Tab
Limited-Access Admin cannot accidentally discover restricted controls
testCases.postconditions: Restricted controls are properly hidden from assistive technology
